text:
Maya: Heads-up, UX check on the model catalog: the two-column preview (filters left / compare right) is collapsing poorly on 1280px. Table squeezes metrics. Thinking of moving filters into a slim sticky chip row above the table on medium screens. Thoughts?

Juan: I mocked a chip-strip that replaces groups when space is tight. Chips are horizontally scrollable; overflow menu holds less-used groups. GIF is in the Figma comment.

Kevin: Nice. How will this affect pin behavior? If I pin a version from a row, will the chip reflect that? Right now pinning only affects the table column.

Maya: Good question. Options: 1) keep pins table-only, 2) mirror pinned state on chips too. I prefer mirroring for quick context.

Aria: Accessibility: chips must be keyboard operable and announce state. Use role=button or native button, aria-pressed, and visible focus. If pins mirror on chips, add sr-only text like "Pinned".

Juan: Agree. My prototype uses an inline 12px pin icon but with a 24px click target. For keyboard: tabindex=0 + Enter/Space handler. Example snippet: 

Juan: ```html
<button class="catalog-chip" aria-pressed="true" aria-label="Version v2.0, pinned">
  v2.0 <svg class="pin-icon" aria-hidden="true"></svg>
</button>
```

Kevin: Also, performance badges in compare rows are crowded (latency / cost / throughput). Could we condense into a single "Perf" token that expands in-row on click? Tooltip-only is fragile for keyboard/screen reader users.

Maya: I like an in-row expand (chevron on the Perf token). Expands inline beneath the row to show the metrics. Need to ensure it doesn't reflow other rows too aggressively.

Aria: Inline expansion is okay if: 1) aria-expanded toggles, 2) the expanded region gets focusable controls, 3) we respect prefers-reduced-motion and animate height only when allowed, 4) use live region announcements for open/close.

DesignBot: Accessibility checklist idea: "Chip buttons have aria-pressed and focus ring; Perf token is a toggle with aria-expanded; Inserts or removes of pinned columns should be announced via an aria-live polite region; All interactive icons have at least 24x24 keyboard targets and contrast >= 4.5:1."

Juan: One implementation snag: inserting a pinned column will shift horizontal scroll and can throw off the user's selection. Plan: calculate new scrollLeft and animate insertion while temporarily locking pointer events to prevent accidental clicks.

Kevin: If a pinned column appears at the left, we need a microcopy change. Current verb "Pin" is ambiguous. Suggest "Pin version" for the action label and tooltip.

Maya: Agreed. Also decision: when filters are collapsed into chips, should pinned badges still show on the compare rows? I want both: a pinned column AND a tiny badge on the chip for quick glance.

Aria: Showing badges in both places is fine but duplicate announcements could be noisy. Use single announcements: "Version v2.0 pinned to comparison." Only announce on the state change, not both UI elements.

Juan: Dev estimate: if we reuse compare layout pieces, chip strip + perf-token + pinned-column animation ~ 3 dev days + 1 QA day for a11y checks. I'll prototype the JS for keyboard handling.

Maya: I'll update Figma with: sticky chip strip, persistent pin icon on chips with sr-only text, consolidated Perf token with chevron expand, pinned-column insertion animation, and aria-live messages.

Kevin: Quick UI nit: when Perf expands, show small inline sparklines for latency distribution and a big number for median latency. Keep colors semantic and accessible.

Aria: Also add a keyboard hint in the expanded region: "Press Esc to close" and trap focus inside until close. Ensure Escape works.

Juan: Will do. Also making overflow menu keyboard-accessible with roving-tabindex for the menu items.

DesignBot: Scheduling: follow-up design + a11y review Thursday 11am PT. Checklist posted in the Figma file.

Maya: Thanks everyone. Uploading updated frames now and will ping when ready.

Kevin: :thumbsup:

Aria: Adding items to accessibility checklist and will run a quick VoiceOver pass after frames land.

Juan: Prototype coming later today.
